title: Vanderbilt BIEN Lab SOZ Resting State SEEG Classification (processed resting-state SEEG)
description: Processed resting-state stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from 79 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy evaluated at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Each patient contributed five minutes of awake, eyes-closed interictal data, filtered and stored in a bipolar montage, with region-level seizure onset zone (SOZ) labels based on Desikan-Killiany parcellation. The data accompany a deep learning study that classifies SOZ versus non-SOZ brain regions from brief interictal recordings.
methods_description: Five minutes of awake, eyes-closed resting-state SEEG were recorded per patient, at least 4 hours from electroclinical seizure activity. Signals were converted to a bipolar montage of adjacent contacts and filtered with MATLAB filtfilt Butterworth passbands (1-59, 61-119, 121-150 Hz). Contacts were localized on post-implantation CT with CRAVE and assigned to Desikan-Killiany regions. SOZs were defined per region as regions containing any contact involved in the ictal onset of at least one seizure.
